A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.15. Text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original toy-model experiments, LLM first-letter classification, absorption measurements, and causal interventions, including additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original toy-model and LLM experiments, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The SAE procedures, sparse probing, absorption-rate definition, and latent-ablation steps are unchanged. Algorithm 1 gains line numbers without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the same synthetic-feature experiments and English-token first-letter/full-spelling evaluations, including appendix variants. No dataset, task, or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same LR-probe and SAE-latent comparisons remain in Section 5.1, alongside the unchanged cosine-similarity versus k=1 sparse-probing comparison in Appendix A.7.

E3.justification: Both retain the 80/20 probe split, model and SAE configurations, training budgets, evaluation metrics, sampling cap of 200 false negatives per letter, and absorption-detection thresholds.

E4.justification: The _short ablation/projection case study, partial-absorption toy experiments, first-letter interventions, and metric comparisons are retained. Section 5.2's rewording describes the existing experiments.

E5.justification: Statistical summaries and their reporting are unchanged. v6 adds no run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the main and appendix plots retain their results. For example, latent 6510 still has F1 of 0.81, and Figure 9b retains the finding of higher absorption with greater sparsity and width.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 retains assumptions H1–H5, the delta-absorption parameterization, both propositions, and the corollary. The mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged despite typesetting adjustments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about sparsity-driven absorption under hierarchical co-occurrence, the detection metric, and validation across hundreds of SAEs.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including the metric's late-layer restriction and its omission of partial or multiple-latent absorption discussed in Section 7 and Appendices A.12–A.13.

D1.justification: Section 1 adds a link to the lasr-spelling/sae-spelling code repository and changes the explorer address from absorption.streamlit.app to feature-absorption.streamlit.app. Implementation, training, and hardware details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 32 cited works and the same positioning relative to SAE evaluation, feature splitting, and Meta-SAEs remain. Bibliography reflow does not change citation membership.

P1.justification: v6 updates affiliations, conference identification, and funding acknowledgments, and makes localized wording edits, including a forward reference to Section 5.2. The section order and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 gains line numbers, Figure 1's placement on page 2 shifts, and the author block, equations, and surrounding text undergo small spacing and reflow changes. Figures and tables retain their content and organization.

improvement.justification: The newly documented project repository in Section 1 improves reproducibility guidance compared with v5's explorer-only access statement. Together with funding disclosures and small clarity edits, this provides a limited quality gain; the scientific evidence, theory, and limitations remain unchanged.
